batchName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE) - Medium Batch 2
chapterName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE)

questions.question: Roughly how many of the 40,000 Romans at the Trebia fought their way out?
questions.explanation: The Romans were surrounded on ground of Hannibal's choosing, and only about a quarter escaped. Afterwards Gauls flocked to Hannibal's army.
questions.sourceQuote: The Carthaginians surrounded the Romans, and only about 10,000 of 40,000 fought their way out.

questions.question: How is Varro, one of the two consuls for 216 BC, described?
options: A Greek-educated senator who sought peace
A veteran general who backed Fabius's strategy
An aristocrat who favoured a middle course
A former dictator recalled from Sicily
A man of reportedly humble origins demanding aggressive war
questions.explanation: Varro reportedly came from humble origins and demanded an aggressive war. His aristocratic colleague favoured a middle course.
questions.sourceQuote: For 216 BC the voters elected two consuls: Varro, a man of reportedly humble origins who demanded an aggressive war, and an aristocratic colleague who favoured a middle course.

questions.question: Why might Polybius's account of Cannae be biased?
options: His patron was the grandson of the consul killed there
He wrote under the emperor Augustus
He relied only on Carthaginian sources
He had served as an officer under Hannibal
questions.explanation: Polybius's patron descended from Varro's colleague, the consul who died at Cannae. His account also survives only in fragments after 216 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: But his account survives only in fragments after 216 BC, and his patron was the grandson of the consul killed at Cannae.

questions.question: Which assets did the Barcas' Spanish domain give Carthage? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Years of mountain fighting won a near-royal domain that supplied silver, farmland, shipyards and soldiers. Before that, Carthage had held only a few coastal towns in Spain.
questions.sourceQuote: It gave Carthage silver mines, rich farmland, shipyards and a deep pool of recruits.

questions.question: What did researchers report finding in peat bogs near the Col de la Traversette? (select all that apply)
options: Soil heavily churned by animals and people
The bones of a war elephant
Unusual levels of horse and mule gut bacteria
questions.explanation: The researchers reported churned soil and unusual levels of gut bacteria from horses and mules, dated to around 218 BC. No weapons or camps have been found on any route.
questions.sourceQuote: Researchers studying peat bogs on both sides of its summit found soil heavily churned, they argue, by thousands of animals and people.

questions.question: Whom did Hannibal place in the crescent-shaped centre of his line at Cannae?
options: Gauls and Spaniards, with himself among them
questions.explanation: Gauls and Spaniards held the centre, which bulged toward the enemy and was meant to give ground. Veteran African infantry waited at either end.
questions.sourceQuote: He placed Gauls and Spaniards in the centre, bulging toward the enemy in a crescent, and stood among them himself.

questions.question: Why did Hannibal free captured Roman allies after his early victories and send them home?
options: Because he could not feed them
To honour the terms of the Ebro Treaty
To exchange them for Carthaginian prisoners
To recruit them as guides over the Apennines
questions.explanation: Hannibal sent Rome's Italian allies home to praise Carthage, hoping to break up Rome's alliance. Roman prisoners, by contrast, were treated harshly.
questions.sourceQuote: Hannibal hoped to pull Rome's alliance apart.

questions.question: Which places went over to Hannibal after Cannae? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Capua, Italy's second city, and the port of Tarentum both defected to Hannibal. Rome had lost perhaps 150,000 men in just 20 months.
questions.sourceQuote: Capua, Italy's second city, and the port of Tarentum went over to Hannibal.

questions.question: Where did a Roman army land in 218 BC, only to miss Hannibal as he passed?
questions.explanation: The Roman army landed at Massalia, a Greek city that is now Marseille, but Hannibal had already slipped past. He then crossed the Rhône and pushed on toward the Alps.
questions.sourceQuote: A Roman army that landed at Massalia, a Greek city now Marseille, missed him.

questions.question: Which Alpine pass has recently gained ground as Hannibal's likely route?
questions.explanation: The Col de la Traversette, on the modern French-Italian border, is now a leading candidate. Sceptics still argue the evidence is too thin to be certain.
questions.sourceQuote: Recently the Traversette, on the modern French-Italian border, has gained ground.
